The main takeaway from our work is that
the subgrid-scale model can be made to be scale invariant, which is a very important feature for large-eddy simulations.

the multifractal model provides a simple and accurate approach for modeling subgrid stresses, and that it is a viable alternative to the eddy viscosity approach, especially for flows with large anisotropy and/or strong shear.

the multifractal subgrid-scale model is able to capture the correct balance between energy transfer and dissipation, and thus the correct energy spectra, in large-eddy simulations of homogeneous isotropic turbulence at a wide range of Reynolds numbers, including those relevant to atmospheric and oceanic flows.
